units.translation: Hesychius ἀγρέμονα [the hunter] (thus Musurus for ἄγρεμον): τὸν κάμακα [the pole] (this can mean either a stake or a spear), from ἀγρεῖν [to hunt] (thus Nanckius for αἴρειν) and λαμβάνειν [to take], that is, ἀγρεύειν [to hunt]. The torch, or spear. Aeschylus in Myrmidons (fr. 138) uses ἀγρέμονα [the hunter] for τὸν ἐπιμήνιον [the monthly priest]. The words ἀγρέμονα τὸν ἐπιμήνιον are separated in the codex as a gloss, by an error, as the particle δέ clearly shows. After τὸν ἐπιμήνιον some substantive seems to have fallen out. Meursius in Graecia Feriata s.v. Νουμηνία [New Moon] understood a sacrificer.
to take, that is, to hunt. The torch, or spear. Aeschylus in Myrmidons

Thus Toupius Emend. vol. 3 p. 353 corrected what is in M ἀγρόται [rustics], with a bad conjecture γρ. άκρόται [marginal reading: topmost] added, which is explained in the scholium γρ. καὶ ἀκρόται, ἐξ οῦ ἔσται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἄκρου· εἰ δὲ ἀγρόται, ἀπὸ τοῦ ἄγειν καὶ ἀγείρειν [marginal reading: and topmost, from which it would be from the top; but if rustics, from leading and gathering], and in the interlinear gloss οἱ ἄρχοντες· εἰ δὲ ἀκρόται, οἱ ἄκροι [the rulers; but if topmost, the topmost]. Since leaders are said to gather an army or host, it follows that the leaders themselves should be called ἀγρέτας [leaders], just as ἱππαρέτης [cavalry leader] is said for leader of cavalry. Hesychius noted ἀγρέταν: ἡγεμόνα, θεόν [leader, god]. Another example of the corrupt reading ἀγρότης [rustic] is in the fragments of Alcman from the Paris papyrus edited by Egger and again collated with the codex by F. Blass in Ritschl's Rheinisches Museum vol. 25 p. 183 [καὶ στρατῶ] ΤΟΝ ΑΓΡΟΤΑΝ [and the army] THE RUSTIC.
For they have gone, the leaders of the army.
